Attachments: Redwood_Soc2_Summary_20261231.pdf (short summary), we’ll follow with the full report once NDA is complete.

Hi Victor / Anika — looping in technical details and answers to a few quick items (high-level; will fill the questionnaire workbook with direct answers):

- SOC 2: attached is a short summary (Redwood_Soc2_Summary_20261231.pdf). Full SOC 2 Type II report for Hosted API is available under NDA. We completed the Type II attestation for control period ending 2026-12-31.

- Encryption: All customer data is encrypted in-transit (TLS 1.2+) and at-rest using AES-256. For Hosted, we manage keys via our cloud KMS; for Private deployments we support customer-managed keys (bring-your-own-KMS) and HSM integrations for FIPS-140-2 compliance.

- Key management / HSM: Yes — Private deployments support KMIP-compatible HSMs or cloud KMS with BYOK. We can provide a deployment checklist for KMS integration.

- Incident response / pen test cadence: IR runbooks + table-top exercises annually; 24/7 on-call security ops with initial triage SLA of 4 hours for critical incidents. Pen tests annually and after major infra changes; we can share recent pen test summary under NDA.

- Data retention / deletion: Configurable per-customer retention policy for logs and KV cache; API-level deletion endpoints and documented procedures for complete data purge in Private.

- HIPAA / BAA: We execute BAAs for customers running PHI on Private deployments; Hosted HIPAA support is available via dedicated environments — we can go into details in the deep-dive.

I’ve started filling the questionnaire and attached our working answers (Redwood_Sec_Answers_EnterpriseCorp_20270216.docx). Expect a completed pass (with Rishi’s technical verifications) by Mon, Feb 21.

Next steps I recommend:
- NDA execution (we can provide standard mutual NDA; prefer DocuSign for speed).
- Security deep-dive Tue, Feb 22 @ 11:00 AM PST — agenda: SOC 2 scope, deployment topology options (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private), KMS/HSM integration, data residency, and timelines for certifications (ISO/FedRAMP).

Let me know if you want us to pre-seed the questionnaire with specific substantiating artifacts.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Victor / Anika — a couple of technical notes from the solutions side ahead of the deep-dive:

- Deployment options: For PHI we typically recommend Private (customer VPC / on-prem) with BYOK and optional air-gapped modes. Dedicated is a good middle-ground for predictable throughput with tenant isolation.
- FedRAMP: If EnterpriseCorp requires FedRAMP Moderate/High, that typically involves GovCloud partner hosting and a certification effort that can take 9–12 months (scope dependent). We can provide a program plan if this is a hard requirement.
- Telemetry & logs: We offer token-level request tracing in the Console and can ship aggregated logs to customer SIEMs via secure forwarders; for Private you can centralize logs to your own collection.
- Quantization / model controls: We can pin specific model versions and quantization profiles for production workloads to lock down reproducible outputs — useful for regulated pipelines.

I’ll be on the deep-dive next week to walk architecture and help validate questionnaire answers.

Thanks,
Rishi Malhotra
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
